program.name: Anthropic Fellows
program.roundStatusEvidence: "Applications are now open for our January cohort - apply here." ... "We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis." (Greenhouse posting; "apply here" = bit.ly/afpsafety, which 301-redirects to the Airtable form). The form itself is published and accepting responses (form config: isClosed false; last published 2026-09-17).
program.nextRoundNote: Rolling admissions; "We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis." No deadline stated for the January 2027 cohort.
program.locationNotes: Shared workspaces in Berkeley and London where fellows work and mentors visit; "We are also open to remote fellows in the UK, US, or Canada." Fellows must be located in the country where they hold full-time work authorization; if authorized in the UK or USA, Anthropic prefers London or Berkeley. No visa sponsorship. Form asks whether you can work from London/Berkeley for the entire program or 25%+ of it.
program.compensation: Weekly stipend of 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD + benefits (vary by country); compute funding ~$15k/month plus other research expenses
program.commitment: Full-time (40 hours/week) for 4 months (possible extension); shorter commitments reviewed case-by-case
eligibilityNotes: Must have or independently obtain full-time work authorization in the US, UK, or Canada and be located in that country during the program; visas are not sponsored.
Must be fluent in Python programming and available to work full-time on the program.
No PhD, prior ML experience, or publications required (alignment.anthropic.com post); strong technical background in CS, math, or physics is listed as a fit signal.
If you cannot commit to the full 4 months, apply anyway and note constraints; reviewed case-by-case.
At least three references required; they may be contacted without notice and asked to respond within a week.

aiPolicy.summary: Applicants must write their own first draft of resume/application answers and may then use Claude (or other AI) to refine it; take-home assessments and live interviews are AI-free unless stated, and the form requires a "Yes" confirmation that the applicant reviewed this policy.
aiPolicy.quote: Please create your first draft yourself, then use Claude to refine it.

stages.name: Initial application
stages.description: Single Airtable form (administered by Constellation): CV (PDF), links, motivation and research-interest answers, full-time/stream likelihood estimates, three references with background and relationship context, stream choices, and logistics (availability, residence, work authorization, workspace location, other commitments).

stages.name: Reference check
stages.description: "The interview process will include an initial application & reference check..." References may be contacted without notice and asked to respond within a week.

stages.name: Technical assessments & interviews
stages.description: Named in the posting; content not published. Per Anthropic AI guidance, take-home assessments are completed without Claude unless indicated, and live interviews without AI assistance.

stages.name: Research discussion
stages.description: Named in the posting as the final step; content not published.

program.notes: Scope: the Airtable form is the safety/security application (stream options: AI Safety & Alignment; AI Safety: Mechanistic Interpretability & Model Internals; AI Security & Frontier Red Team). The safety posting says all applicants currently use the same portal, but the ML Systems & RL posting routes to its own Greenhouse application. Form has 47 input fields, 30 required; 3 are conditional (one effectively unreachable). The internal Airtable page name is "Anthropic Fellows | Applications closed" but its close flag is false and the form renders a working Submit button, so it is treated as open. Non-input submission terms at the end of the form: "By submitting this application:" you consent to your information being shared with Constellation; you agree the information is accurate and "The submitted work samples represent your own work; for any co-authored work you have described your contribution, and you have permission to share the materials." Length guidance on three questions is given in paragraphs (recorded with unit "items").
